the development of a high-density oligo-nucleotide microarray for the assessment of gene transcription from pelagic microbial communities in the world’s oceans.

the MicroTOOLs array is a powerful tool for characterizing the functional responses of diverse pelagic microbial taxa to environmental change.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MicroTOOLs is an open-access resource that can be used to study microbial functional gene expression in a wide range of environments.
the MicroTOOLs design provides a robust tool to characterize the functional potential of major microbial groups in the open ocean.

we designed a microarray that targets 19 000 unique sequences from 145 genes across all three domains of life, and we used it in a proof-of-principle experiment that showed transcriptional responses of microbial communities to nutrient additions in the North Pacific Gyre.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metatranscriptomics can provide a powerful tool for understanding how microbial communities respond to environmental change, and that MicroTOOLs is a useful platform to explore this response.
the design and implementation of MicroTOOLs is a model that can be applied to other environments to address a range of research questions.
